text:
sarah: Heads up — product wants a straightforward mapping between quota tiers and plan labels for the console (free / pro / enterprise). They also want to surface a per-org 'burst pool' and how it's split per API key. Quick thoughts?

mike: +1. We currently have internal tier ids (free=0, pro=10, ent=100). Billing returns those ids. Console just shows labels today. We need a deterministic mapping to avoid surprises when plans change. :thinking_face: 

jen: We should avoid exposing raw ids. Instead compute a presentation object server-side: {label, token_hour_rate, burst_capacity, per_key_softcap}. Example:  "presentationTier": "Pro" etc. That keeps UI logic simple.

robin: Agreed. UX note: show an estimated "available burst" number per org and then show per-key share when keys >1. People get confused by percentages. Suggest: show absolute tokens + percentage.

kevin: Implementation detail: where should mapping live? Options: billing service (authoritative), quota service (enforcement), or a small kit in console code (fast but risk drift). I vote billing service + cache in quota service.

jersey: (I typo'd earlier — meant jen) For calculations, propose formula in billing svc: 
```
org_burst = min(plan_max_burst, committed_pool - used_this_window)
per_key_share = floor(org_burst / max(active_keys,1))
visible_value = {org_burst, per_key_share}
```
This keeps enforcement separate.

ops-bot: deploy @quota-service v2.9 started by kevin — rolling 3 pods.

mike: One more: fallback behavior. If quota svc cannot reach billing for mapping, show cached mapping + banner: "plan details may be stale". Don't fall back to zeros.

alyssa: Telemetry ask: emit event `quota.mapping.render` with fields [org_id, plan_label, cached:true|false, active_keys_count, per_key_share] so product can analyze confusion metrics.

jen: Also surface a small tooltip explaining "burst pool is shared across keys; keys get equal split unless reserved allocations exist". Example tooltip copy: "Burst pool: temporary extra tokens usable at short notice. These are shared by all keys on this org — view per-key allocation above."

elaine: Rollouts: let's feature-flag the console change. Start with 10% of orgs (exclude enterprise for accuracy), monitor `quota.mapping.render` and `quota.enforcement.fallthrough` for errors, then ramp.

sarah: Sounds actionable. Next steps: (1) kevin files an RFC to put mapping in billing service + API contract, (2) jen drafts the tooltip + UI copy, (3) alyssa wires telemetry, (4) robin designs UX mockup. I'll coordinate rollout window after RFC. :+1:

kevin: I'll open the RFC today and add an example response shape. Will include TTL for cached entries and a compatibility guard for older quota svc.

jen: I'll drop the copy in #design and link mockups.

mike: I'll add a short circuit in quota svc to use cached values when billing unreachable. Will also add logs for mismatch errors.

sarah: Great. Thanks everyone — tagging follow-ups: @kevin @jen @alyssa @robin.

ops-bot: deploy @console-web v3.2 scheduled in 2 hours for canary group (10% traffic).
